local_checks.invariant: No eval()/Function()/child_process sink consumes runtime-attacker-controlled code.
local_checks.result: Covered: three eval() families exist but none takes request/message-level attacker code: (1) SSR buildQuery evals base64 getContextValue_ markers that come from the compiled query.graphql build artifact, not from HTTP input; (2) promotion condition evaluators run eval on numeric operands and a hard-coded comparison-operator set, with conditions authored by the admin and prices from DB numerics; (3) dynamic import of extensions resolves operator-configured filesystem paths. secureFetch enforces an IMAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS allowlist on every redirect hop (SSRF defense).

local_checks.invariant: Cookies carry HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite; CORS is not wildcard-permitting credentials; no open redirect params; TLS enforced in production.
local_checks.result: Hardening drift: express-session default httpOnly=true, but sess.cookie.secure=true is explicitly overridden to false in production (addDefaultMiddlewareFuncs.ts:85-88), SameSite is never set, and saveUninitialized defaults to true (configExample says false - example/dev value). No CORS middleware exists anywhere (no wildcard ACAO, browser same-origin applies). No redirect-style query params feeding res.redirect() in modules. Session cookie is therefore transmissible over plaintext HTTP - attacker needs a cookie-reading/Set-Cookie primitive (see cookie-secret hardening note, chained).

local_checks.invariant: The SSR query assembler's eval() must never receive runtime attacker-controlled text.

local_checks.invariant: A forged signed cookie or unverified/expired JWT must not establish a current user; account deactivation/role changes must take effect promptly.

local_checks.invariant: Refresh tokens are long-lived, single-secret, never rotated, never revoked, not bound to a session/access token
local_checks.result: generateRefreshToken has no jti/family/kid/session anchor; verifyRefreshToken only checks sig/iss/aud/tokenType/tokenKind. Refresh endpoints mint a NEW access token only; the old refresh token stays valid and replayable until expiry (admin 54000s=15h, customer 108000s=30h) and survives password changes. A leaked refresh token continuously mints access tokens; sessionTokens.ts additionally converts an admin session cookie into a JWT pair. [check verdict: needs_validation]

local_checks.invariant: Per-IP quota accounting keys on an identity dimension the requester cannot influence (real client IP), and one principal must not be able to spend another principal's budget.
local_checks.result: Invariant fails at the rendered default: trust proxy numeric hop-count (default 1) makes the direct socket peer the trusted hop, so request.ip becomes the first client-supplied X-Forwarded-For entry; express-rate-limit 8.7.0 keys the MemoryStore buckets on req.ip. In the compose deploy (direct :3000 publish, TRUST_PROXY_HOPS unset) an unauthenticated caller can rotate XFF to dodge every tier (page 300/60s, api 120/60s, auth 8/15min) and can pin a victim IP to burn its auth attempts (login lockout). Candidate rate-limit.credential-endpoints.missing-auth-tier.jwt-mint.

local_checks.invariant: The upload mimetype allowlist is the effective gate preventing script-capable files (SVG and executables) from being stored; it must hold against adversarial content, not only client-declared strings.
local_checks.result: fileFilter (getMulter.js:157-163) accepts a file when getAllowedMimeTypes().includes(file.mimetype) — file.mimetype is multer/busboy's client-declared part Content-Type. No content/magic-byte inspection exists anywhere on the write path; generateFileName preserves the client-supplied extension (generateFileName.js:3-9); localUploader writes the buffer verbatim under MEDIAPATH (uploadFile.ts:70-101); static.ts ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS includes .svg/.js/.json (static.ts:10-46) and serves MEDIAPATH (static.ts:130-137). The explicit stated intent of the allowlist (SVG 'deliberately absent — XSS vector when served', getMulter.js:7-10) is therefore not enforced against adversarial multipart content. All upload endpoints are access:private and gated by the API auth middleware (auth/api/global/[getCurrentUser]auth.ts:11-30), so planting requires an admin credential; the resulting file is served to anonymous storefront visitors at /assets/media/...; the only headers set are X-Content-Type-Options nosniff and cache headers (static.ts:87-89), which do not neutralize active script on direct/iframe navigation to an image/svg+xml resource. Runtime proof of the multipart forgery and the served Content-Type is external to this repo (no deps vendored) and cannot be executed here.

local_checks.invariant: Files may only be read/written/deleted/browsed under MEDIAPATH; path traversal must be rejected on the actual join result.
local_checks.result: validatePath (validatePath.js:3-16) checks joinedPath.startsWith(root) — a raw string prefix, not a path-component boundary — so a request like '../media2/x' joins to '<root>/media2/x', which string-prefix-matches root '<root>/media', and cleanPath===normalizedPath also passes. The upload middleware neutralizes this with an additional /^[a-zA-Z0-9_\/-]+$/i regex (fileUpload/[auth,validatePath]multerFile.js:5-6) and folderCreate repeats the regex; fileBrowser and fileDelete apply ONLY validatePath, so GET/DELETE /api/files/../media2/x pass the gate. Reachable impact is confined to (a) admin-authenticated callers — both routes are access:private behind the API auth gate — and (b) sibling directories whose absolute path shares the MEDIAPATH string prefix and that already exist on disk (default layout has none), so the escaped target set is empty/non-default. Recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: The public /images proxy may only fetch from hosts on the SSRF allowlist, including every redirect hop, and must refuse by default.
local_checks.result: Invariant holds at the hostname level for public reachability: GET /images (route.json, no auth in the pages region) funnels src through secureFetch (imageProcessor.ts:222). assertAllowedUrl restricts protocol to http(s) and compares url.hostname against getAllowedImageHosts() (env IMAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS + registered providers) after stripping IPv6 brackets (secureFetch.ts:96-113); guardedConnector re-checks options.hostname on EVERY connection including each redirect hop (secureFetch.ts:74-88); with no env var/provider the effective list is empty so no external host is reachable at all (secureFetch.ts:35-53, bootstrap.ts:23-60). Provider-derived hosts come only from operator cloud-storage config (storageConfig.ts getFileStorageImageHosts). Residual weaknesses: the allowlist is compared to the hostname STRING only; the IP that DNS resolves to is never validated and ports 80/443 are not restricted, so a rebindable/operator-shadowable allowlisted hostname could reach non-public addresses. These are conditional on deployment allowlist contents and require runtime confirmation of undici connect/DNS behavior.

local_checks.invariant: The on-disk derivative cache must stay bounded: a per-key cap, an aggregate cache cap/eviction, and no unbounded key space derived from untrusted input.
local_checks.result: Invariant fails at source. /images (public GET, page-tier rate limit 300/60s per IP — rateLimit.ts classifyRequest) passes attacker-controlled width (unbounded int), optional height (unbounded int), quality (parseInt||75, unbounded), and one of 4 formats straight into imageProcessor (images.ts:10-30). generateCacheKey (imageProcessor.ts:33-46) builds a unique filename from base64(src)-w-h-q.format; on every miss the pipeline decodes the source, resizes/encodes (imageProcessor.ts:289-368), and unconditionally fs.writeFile's the derivative into CACHE_DIR=path.resolve(BUILDPATH,'../images') i.e. <root>/.evershop/images (imageProcessor.ts:174,370-372). Because resizeOption withoutEnlargement (imageProcessor.ts:295) and default input/output pixel caps bound each FILE's size but not the NUMBER of files, one existing source image yields an unbounded set of distinct persistent keys (e.g. all widths below source width, all h values, q 1..N, 4 formats; widths above source width each still write an approximately source-sized file). A grep of the tree finds no eviction, TTL, cap, or cleanup owner for the images cache. Impact: persistent shared-disk growth on the app's own storage volume (filling it stops the whole store), plus per-miss CPU/IO on every unique key. Only control is the per-IP rate limit; concurrency is not capped. Source evidence complete; the concrete throughput/retention demonstration requires a sandboxed fixture that this environment cannot provide.

local_checks.invariant: An untrusted (or barely-trusted) image representation must be bounded at decode/buffer time; SVG rasterization must not disable pixel caps.
local_checks.result: Invariant fails at source on two unbounded-decoding paths. (1) SVG: for any source that sharp reports as SVG, imageProcessor instantiates sharp with density:300 and limitInputPixels:false (imageProcessor.ts:306-313), so an SVG with a large declared canvas rasterizes to a huge pixel buffer with no pixel cap (decompression/representation amplification); for jpeg output an SVG is re-rasterized to png (imageProcessor.ts:274-277). (2) External fetch: secureFetch imposes only a 15s timeout (secureFetch.ts:126) with NO response-body size cap, and imageProcessor buffers the whole response with response.arrayBuffer() (imageProcessor.ts:228-229) before sharp's (capped) decode. Both are reachable without authentication via /images (src selects any local media/public/theme path, or any allowlisted external URL). The SVG path additionally requires an SVG to exist in a readable location (default pool has none; plugin via the unit-1 mimetype-bypass is a compounding precondition). Per-file sharp defaults cap some consequences; the unbounded-cases need a bound fixture to demonstrate exactly.

local_checks.invariant: Reset token is delivered and consumed as a URL query parameter; exposed to Referer/history/logs and rendered into the DOM
local_checks.result: The reset link embeds the 128-hex token as ?token= in the email; the page reads it from window.location.search and puts it in a hidden form input. The app sets no Referrer-Policy, so a same-tab click on an external link while on that page sends the token via Referer; browser history/proxies/access-logs also see it. Token is single-use and 48h-bounded. [check verdict: needs_validation]

local_checks.invariant: Token entropy, hashing, single-use, expiry, and timezone handling are sound
local_checks.result: 64 random bytes (128 hex), stored sha256-hashed, deleted after use, default 48h lifetime enforced on created_at. The naive 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss' literal is compared in the DB session whose TZ is set to shop.timezone (connection.ts onConnect), so no offset drift. Generic 200 response for unknown emails; link base from config/env (no Host-header injection). [check verdict: passed]

local_checks.invariant: Reset email is also sent to addresses with no account (token not persisted => unusable)
local_checks.result: sendResetPasswordEmail is invoked for non-existent customers with a token that is never inserted; harmless but grants a mail-based oracle for enumerating registered emails (rate-limited per IP). [check verdict: note]

local_checks.invariant: Password change does not invalidate existing sessions or JWTs
local_checks.result: updatePassword updates the customer password only; outstanding session cookies and JWT pairs stay valid (ties to units 2/3 invalidation findings). [check verdict: note]

excluded_blocks.reason: Cookie transport hardening is deployment-dependent (see session/cookie unit); not a standalone attack class.

local_checks.invariant: PATCH /customers/me/addresses/:address_id may only update an address owned by the authenticated customer and must not allow the body to change the address owner or identity columns.
local_checks.result: Ownership enforced: the handler selects the address WHERE uuid = :address_id AND customer_id = currentCustomer.customer_id before updating; PROTECTED_FIELDS = [customer_id, customer_address_id, uuid, address_id] are stripped from the request body; the update runs through updateCustomerAddress on the row matched by uuid. customer_address columns contain no other identity/privilege fields. No bypass path found.

local_checks.invariant: Self-service address create/delete must bind writes to the authenticated customer and must not cross customer_id boundaries.
local_checks.result: createMyAddress binds the new row's customer_id to currentCustomer.uuid; deleteMyAddress applies the same uuid + customer_id ownership SELECT before deleting; both strip PROTECTED_FIELDS. No bypass path found.

local_checks.invariant: Admin address endpoints that share the self-service address services must be admin-gated (no weaker-permission path) and must bind the address to the URL customer rather than to a body-supplied owner.
local_checks.result: All three admin route.json are access:'private' (covered by the [getCurrentUser]auth.ts route gate); handlers resolve the customer from request.params.customer_id and bind address operations to that customer_id instead of a caller-controllable owner field. No weaker-permission path found.

local_checks.invariant: Customer self-service endpoints cannot escalate authorization state (group_id, status, password) beyond what the principal may set; public registration must not override privileged fields.
local_checks.result: updateCustomerProfile strips SENSITIVE_FIELDS = [password, group_id, status]. createCustomer (public POST /customers) does persist group_id/status from the request body (customerDataSchema.json additionalProperties:true), but no catalog/checkout pricing consumes customer_group_id at this commit (cart copies customer.group_id into cart.customer_group_id), so no authority impact was established -> hardening note, not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Storefront customer GraphQL must return only the current customer's own data; admin-only customer queries must be excluded from the public schema.
local_checks.result: currentCustomer returns the request-context customer (or null); admin customer rows are in Customer.admin.graphql excluded from the storefront schema (buildTypes ignores only '.admin.graphql'). However the shared oms Order type leaks order queries into the same storefront schema (see orderView check) - surfaced as candidate storefront-order-uuid-unscoped.

local_checks.invariant: The customer orderView page must not render another customer's order; the storefront /graphql endpoint must not return orders without an ownership filter.
local_checks.result: orderView/index.ts gates on customer login then delegates ownership enforcement to the GraphQL resolver (documented as the 'storefront contract' in the same file); Order.resolvers.js:11-20 resolves order(uuid) with only a uuid predicate, getOrdersBaseQuery is an unfiltered select().from('order'), Order.graphql is a shared (non-admin) schema file, and /graphql is access:'public'. Violation established from source; runtime confirmation blocked (no sandbox).

local_checks.invariant: Customer account pages gate on customer login; login and order-tracking flows do not weaken authentication or authorization.
local_checks.result: account, orderList, orderTracking pages gate correctly (orderTracking additionally verifies an HMAC-signed tracking token bound to the order uuid). Two hardening notes: account/index.ts:10-16 skips its login gate for any nonempty ?changeset (enforcePreviewThemeMatch treats a nonexistent token as ok, so anonymous requests render only a data-less shell since currentCustomer is null); loginCustomerWithEmail.ts:13-17 uses ILIKE escaping % but not _.

local_checks.invariant: The public storefront order(uuid) query must not return any order's PII without proving ownership.
local_checks.result: RE-VERIFIED: Query.order is the only order resolver; it resolves via getOrdersBaseQuery() (bare select().from('order'), uuid equality only) with no customer_id predicate; Order.graphql is merged into the public storefront schema because buildTypes.js:19 excludes only *.admin.graphql types and buildResolvers(false) excludes only .admin.resolvers.*. PII server-side fields present (customerEmail, customerFullName, userIp, billing/shipping addresses). DISPOSITION: needs_validation (static trace confirmed; runtime exploitation not executed).

unresolved: Runtime confirmation of storefront-order-uuid-unscoped (anonymous /graphql returning order PII; cross-customer orderView rendering) requires the sandboxed dummy-store check, which is blocked by the no-sandbox rule.
The root-cause file oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js belongs to the oms module and matches parent-verified lead #2 (Order IDOR) - the parent should dedupe.

local_checks.invariant: sign/verify use a dedicated high-entropy secret with pinned algorithm/issuer/audience and no fallback
local_checks.result: HS256 forced at sign and verify; algorithms:['HS256'], issuer 'evershop:tracking', audience 'order-tracking', expiresIn from config (default 90d); secret from ORDER_TRACKING_TOKEN_SECRET only — sign throws, verify returns {ok:false,reason:'no_secret'} when unset; no hardcoded fallback

local_checks.invariant: crypto failure must not fall back to no-crypto or a partial read
local_checks.result: verify failure returns distinct reasons expired/invalid/no_secret; page handler renders the 'no longer valid' view and never loads the order for a failed token; expired vs invalid differentiated (TokenExpiredError catch)

local_checks.invariant: the embedded orderUuid is bound to the requested path so one token cannot open another order
local_checks.result: token orderUuid compared against pathUuid; mismatch yields status 'mismatch' and a rejected view; else page loads the token's orderUuid only

local_checks.invariant: A storefront GraphQL request document is validated against the schema and bounded for depth/complexity/alias/token volume before execution; an invalid or amplification-shaped query must be rejected, not silently executed.
local_checks.result: graphqlMiddleware.js:22 calls validateSchema(schema, document) (validates the SCHEMA, not the document — the query AST is never validated; specifiedRules are never applied). parse(query) at :20 passes no token/size options and execute at :37 applies no depth/complexity/alias bound; no such limit exists anywhere in the module (grep). The storefront schema is self-referential (Category.children/parent/path, Category.graphql:17-19) and Category.children (Category.resolvers.ts:124) executes a per-node DB select, so an unauthenticated sub-100kB POST (route.json access public) can fan out to thousands of DB statements on the shared pool per request. The api rate tier (rateLimit.ts:20, 120/60s/IP) bounds volume, not per-request amplification. Amplification candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Source-visible input caps (body size, rate, framework limits) bound the earliest accepted work before amplification.
local_checks.result: Body cap: bodyParser.json({inflate:false}) with default 100kb (body-parser ^1.20.5); GET /graphql reads an empty body (no-op). Rate cap: api tier 120 req/60s per IP ahead of session/DB work. These bound input SIZE and request VOLUME but not the per-request amplification factor (a ~100kB document already fits thousands of aliases / deep Category recursion).

local_checks.invariant: No middleware or framework guard on the /graphql route rejects or caps adversarial query shapes before execution.
local_checks.result: The route-level chain for /api/graphql is only context/bodyParser/auth-removeUser + graphqlMiddleware; no depth/complexity/alias/introspection gate exists at the framework layer. The auth route gate skips access==='public' routes, so the storefront endpoint is unguarded by design. Admin /admin/graphql uses the same unbounded middleware behind an authenticated gate (same root cause, lower reach). Introspection (__schema) is enabled on the public endpoint.

unresolved: Per-request resolver count / CPU / DB-statement growth curve across alias and depth scaling is only measurable by running the target or a bounded fixture; no OS sandbox is available (recorded in the needs_validation candidate).

local_checks.invariant: Order records returned by the storefront Query.order(uuid) must be bound to the requesting principal (customer/session/anonymous token); a bare uuid must not yield another principal's PII.
local_checks.result: Boundary holds only partially. getOrdersBaseQuery.js:3-6 returns select().from('order') with no ownership predicate; Order.resolvers.js:11-14 adds only where('uuid','=',uuid). Order.graphql:204 exposes order(uuid:String!) in the non-admin (storefront) schema; /api/graphql is access public (route.json:4) and [auth]removeUser sets context.user=undefined, so an unauthenticated caller can read any order's customerEmail/customerFullName/userIp, shippingAddress/billingAddress (fullName/postcode/telephone/address1/address2), items, activities, and shipments. Intended controls exist on sibling paths (Customer.orders scoped by customer_id at Order.resolvers.js:149-155; anonymous tracking binds uuid to a signed token at orderTracking/index.ts:44-68), confirming the resolver-level read is the missing control. Order IDOR candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Cart records returned by storefront Query.cart(id) must be bound to the session/customer that owns the cart; a bare uuid must not yield another shopper's contact/address data or act as a handle to its mutation endpoints.
local_checks.result: Boundary fails. Cart.resolvers.ts:19-25 resolves Query.cart(id) -> getCartByUUID -> getCart (Cart.js:184-188) with only uuid+status predicates, then returns cart.exportData() (customerEmail/customerFullName/userIp and cart_address rows via shippingAddress/billingAddress resolvers) to anyone knowing the uuid. The returned object also exposes addItemApi/checkoutApi/addAddressApi etc. (Cart.resolvers.ts:99-108) that point at public REST handlers keying on cart_id alone (addCartItem/route.json access public; addItemToCart.js:17 getCartByUUID(cartId) with no ownership check). The intended control exists as Query.myCart (Cart.resolvers.ts:27-48), scoped to the signed frontstore session cookie + customer_id. Cart IDOR + chained mutation-handle candidate.

local_checks.invariant: No OTHER storefront (non-admin) Query root returns private per-account records without an ownership predicate.
local_checks.result: Surveyed all non-admin 'extend type Query' files in the storefront schema composition (buildTypes.js excludes only '*.admin.graphql'; buildResolvers(false) excludes only '.admin.resolvers.*' and '.ts'). The only uuid-addressed private-account roots are Query.order and Query.cart. Customer.orders is scoped to the resolved customer; Query.myCart is scoped to the signed session cookie; Order metafields are audience-gated by context.user presence. No additional unscoped root found. No separate finding.

local_checks.invariant: No code path may attach a cart/order to a principal or object it does not own; no request-specified object id may flow into a data access unbound by an ownership predicate.
local_checks.result: RE-VERIFIED: getCartByUUID() is a thin passthrough of the caller uuid into getCart() whose only predicates are uuid=? and status=true (Cart.js:185-186); no handler compares the cart sid/customer_id to the requester. API+graphql routes are stateless (session middleware skips them, addDefaultMiddlewareFuncs.ts:224-225) so no server-side ownership binding exists; guestCheckout gate (orderValidator.ts:117) only hardcodes the auth requirement, it does not bind ownership. DISPOSITION: needs_validation (runtime exploitation not executed; cart uuid is a gen_random_uuid 122-bit secret - mitigant, so exposure depends on uuid leakage).

local_checks.invariant: The public storefront order(uuid) query must not return any order's PII without proving ownership.
local_checks.result: RE-VERIFIED: Query.order is the only order resolver; it resolves via getOrdersBaseQuery() (bare select().from('order'), uuid equality only) with no customer_id predicate; Order.graphql is merged into the public storefront schema because buildTypes.js:19 excludes only *.admin.graphql types and buildResolvers(false) excludes only .admin.resolvers.*. PII server-side fields present (customerEmail, customerFullName, userIp, billing/shipping addresses). DISPOSITION: needs_validation (static trace confirmed; runtime exploitation not executed).

unresolved: Unauthorized read of a victim order/cart row is only observable by running the API (no OS sandbox available) — recorded in the needs_validation candidate records with exact blockers.

local_checks.invariant: No untrusted input may reach a dangerous sink (eval, query/variable structure, URL building) during SSR query assembly; request-derived values may only arrive as data inside quotes and must survive the JSON5 round-trip without escaping it.
local_checks.result: The assembled GraphQL document structure comes from build-time query.graphql artifacts and DB-stored widget settings; attacker input can only appear as request context VALUES serialized into strings/variables. Values are JSON5-stringified and quote-escaped (line 75) before insertion and recovered by JSON5.parse (line 79), so they cannot break out of their string literal. The two eval() sites (lines 69 and 325) execute only base64 tokens that are embedded in build artifacts (getContextValue_/getWidgetSetting_ markers); no traced path lets a visitor influence the decoded expression. request.body.graphqlQuery is overwritten from artifacts, so a crafted POST body on a page route cannot alter the query. No attacker-reachable trust-boundary failure.

local_checks.invariant: The SSR execution path must apply the same validation discipline as the API path so a build-controlled document cannot hide the shared wrong-API misuse.
local_checks.result: [buildQuery]graphql[response].js:47-51 also calls validateSchema(schema, document, specifiedRules...) — the wrong API (validates the schema, not the document) — mirroring graphqlMiddleware.js:22. On the SSR path the document is build-controlled and variables come from request context values only, so no untrusted shaper of the document exists; the flaw is correctness/hardening here, not a candidate. The shared misuse on the public API path is fingerprinted in unit 1.

local_checks.invariant: A lower-trust visitor cannot select the identity of the record the SSR page resolves (order uuid must come from a verified token, not the URL).
local_checks.result: The anonymous tracking page binds the resolved order uuid to a verified HS256 JWT: token absence/expiry/invalidity sets trackingStatus and orderUuid=null (index.ts:33-54), and a path-uuid/token-uuid mismatch is treated as tampering (index.ts:56-65). The route is GET-only and the page never reads an order uuid from query parameters. This path is properly token-gated; the bare order(uuid) read on the public API remains the separate unit-2 candidate.

local_checks.invariant: order status is a function of payment+shipment rollups, moves forward only, and is terminal-sticky
local_checks.result: Hold at source: statusManager registers payment/shipment phases and the oms bootstrap composes ordered psoMapping; updateOrderStatus.ts:105-116 resolves with payment-wildcard-before-shipment precedence and clampOrderStatus (168-186) prevents regressions and terminal re-entry (isTerminalOrderStatus 126-138). No path writes an unregistered or backward status.

local_checks.invariant: shipment phase transitions follow the allowed per-phase map
local_checks.result: Hold at source: updateShipmentStatus.ts:32-36 PHASE_TRANSITIONS table is consulted per request (gate at 174-179) against the per-shipment registry; delivered/canceled are terminal; same-phase is accepted; cancelShipment and markDelivered route through it. No bypass found.

local_checks.invariant: createShipment cannot over-allocate item qty, even concurrently
local_checks.result: Hold at source: createShipment acquires a per-order pg_advisory_xact_lock (createShipment.ts:86-93, taken at 571) and re-validates quantity bounds, canceled-shipment exclusion, and received qty inside the lock at phase 2 (571-579). The shipment path serializes its write decisions.

local_checks.invariant: cancelOrder restock mirrors the placement deduction (manage_stock guard, shipped/delivered exclusion) and honors the restock-on-cancel configuration
local_checks.result: Violated at source: the placement-time deduct trigger guards `AND manage_stock = TRUE` (Version-1.0.0.js:278, Version-1.0.2.js:13), but cancelOrder.ts reStockAfterCancel (115-129) re-adds the full order_item.qty for every item with no manage_stock guard and no subtraction of already shipped/delivered quantity; the `oms.order.reStockAfterCancellation` config is registered (bootstrap.ts:213, default true at 371) but is never read anywhere in core; payment-status cancelability keeps shipped/partially_delivered rollups cancelable (bootstrap.ts:359-370, documented in cancelOrderValidate.test.js). See candidate oms.cancelOrder.restock-asymmetric.

local_checks.invariant: a refund cannot exceed the captured amount, even under concurrent requests
local_checks.result: Violated at source: refundOrder.ts checks isRefundable (62-66), computes remainingRefundableMinorUnits from a pre-read SELECT (69-90), then calls the gateway (factory.refund 94-99), and only afterwards recordRefund.ts writes in its own short transaction (77-125) re-deriving totals (101) without an atomic cap; the payment path has no per-order advisory lock (contrast pg_advisory_xact_lock in createShipment.ts:90/571). Concurrent refunds race past the same gate. See candidate oms.refundOrder.amount-race.

local_checks.invariant: an authorization is gateway-captured at most once
local_checks.result: Violated at source: captureOrder.ts gates on isCapturable (63) from a status read, selects the authorization transaction without a lock (71-79), calls factory.capture (85) before any DB write, then records the capture and payment_status in a short transaction (95-113); there is no conditional state transition on payment_status, so two concurrent captures can both pass the gate and both invoke the gateway. See candidate oms.captureOrder.state-race.

unresolved: The payment provider adapter selected at runtime (stripe/paypal) decides whether a second gateway capture or refund actually settles money (external idempotency behavior).
The availability impact of restocked delivered stock depends on storefront runtime evaluation of the inventory flag (ProductCollection.js predication), reproducible only at deployment.

local_checks.invariant: Every non-public API route must require an authenticated admin identity; a route with no access property must be treated as private.
local_checks.result: Drop-in route gate: currentRoute.access === 'public' is the only bypass; routes with no access key default to private in scanForRoutes; otherwise currentAdminUser.uuid is required and roles ('*' default, or comma-separated route-id membership) are checked. The middleware is scope 'app', region 'api', so it mounts on every API route. No un-gated API route found.

local_checks.invariant: Admin API authentication cannot be satisfied with a customer token, another audience/kind, or a customer-controlled role claim.
local_checks.result: The JWT path skips tokens whose tokenType is not ADMIN; verifyToken checks tokenType, tokenKind, audience and issuer against the admin secret; roles are built server-side from the admin_user row (roles || '*'). No client-controlled role escalation and no admin/customer token confusion.

local_checks.invariant: All OMS, setting and catalog API routes that mutate or read operational data must carry access 'private' (or otherwise meet the gate).
local_checks.result: Audited every route.json under the trees: 14/14 oms/api private (cancelOrder, cancelShipment, captureOrder, createOrderRefund, createShipment, lifetimesales, listOrderShipments, markDelivered, markShipmentDelivered, salestatistic, updateOrderMetafields, updateShipmentByUuid, updateShipment, voidShipmentLabel); setting/api/saveSetting private; catalog/api 27/27 private. Zero 'public' routes in these trees.

local_checks.invariant: Admin SSR pages (oms/pages/admin, setting/pages/admin) must be reachable only by an authenticated, active admin session.
local_checks.result: Admin pages are registered via registerAdminRoute with no access key (private by default) and the region-pages gate (auth/pages/admin/all/[context]auth.js, routeId 'admin') redirects unauthenticated users to the admin login and rejects disabled admins. No bypass found.

local_checks.invariant: Admin GraphQL must be private, and the storefront GraphQL endpoint must not expose admin-only operations or otherwise bypass the route gate.
local_checks.result: /admin/graphql is access 'private' (gate applies). /graphql is access 'public' and intentionally passes the gate; its exposure is limited to the storefront schema, but that schema carries the unscoped oms Order query (cross-unit root cause, parent lead #2) - recorded as uncovered, not as an oms-admin gate failure. Appendix (was unresolved): OMS handlers (cancelOrder, createOrderRefund, updateShipmentByUuid, salestatistic, lifetimesales, saveSetting) perform no per-object authorization beyond the route gate; this matches the documented single-admin 'no RBAC' architecture and is recorded as a hardening note.

local_checks.invariant: a preview token binds possession to a real changeset and carries sufficient entropy
local_checks.result: isValidPreviewToken is a parameterized SELECT 1 FROM changeset WHERE token=$1; token is a uuidv4 (128-bit) generated per (admin, theme) draft — possession-based model, unguessable tokens

local_checks.invariant: preview overlays render only under the changeset's theme, decided per request storefront-wide
local_checks.result: middleware mounted on all frontStore routes; no token = no-op; mismatch returns 409 (JSON/XHR) or 302 to '/' — enforced at both request edge and loadActiveOps

local_checks.invariant: production overlay applies only active rollout ops within their time window, theme, and route cursor; in-progress editor edits do not leak live
local_checks.result: production branch filters start_time<=NOW()<end_time, theme match, and rp.route_cursors per op.route; preview branch returns only the token's changeset ops inside cs.route_cursors — no accounting drift found

local_checks.invariant: draft mutations require admin auth, own the draft, respect published-state and theme scope
local_checks.result: each API verifies admin_user_id and rejects foreign drafts (isForeignDraft), published changesets, and cross-theme UPDATE/DELETE targets; publish is transactional and preserves the changeset for audit

local_checks.invariant: the sitemap search-index copy reflects current lifecycle state (status + schedule + active theme) and is invalidated on lifecycle change
local_checks.result: landing-pages collector filters status=true AND window (COALESCE NOW() bounds) AND active-theme placement in BOTH collect() and getFingerprint(); the fingerprint folds in the same filtered source so a schedule boundary moving past NOW() forces regeneration at the cron cadence; served with public max-age=3600 — bounded staleness only, no in-repo perpetual stale listing

local_checks.invariant: responses that reveal lifecycle-bound content (draft/out-of-window previews, schedule-windowed landing pages) carry explicit cache-control/noindex so no shared copy outlives the ACL window
local_checks.result: SSR full-page responses set no Cache-Control and no X-Robots-Tag; preview responses render at the REAL canonical /<key> URL with full page meta; no in-repo HTML cache exists (only images/blogRss/sitemap set Cache-Control) — the copy lifecycle is left entirely to external caches → candidate (needs_validation)

unresolved: deployment fact not source-visible: whether a shared/edge HTML cache exists and whether it stores responses that carry a Set-Cookie session header or strips query strings for cache keys; and the actual response headers produced by the running storefront for live vs preview URLs

local_checks.invariant: orderUuidLookup in createPaymentIntent binds the order to the current principal (session/cart/customer) before minting a PaymentIntent
local_checks.result: Control ABSENT. route.json declares access 'public'; the API auth gate ([getCurrentUser]auth.ts:18) passes public routes with next(); the select at createPaymentIntent.ts:29-34 filters only on uuid + payment_method='stripe' + payment_status='pending'. Any caller who knows a pending Stripe order id can mint an intent and receives its client_secret. Following inputs traced: request.body order_id -> unscoped select -> stripe.paymentIntents.create -> client_secret returned to the (unauthenticated) caller.

local_checks.invariant: the charged amount must come from the frozen server-side order, never from the client
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT. amount = toStripeMinorUnit(order.grand_total, order.currency), currency = order.currency, and metadata.order_id = order.uuid are all read from the loaded order row (createPaymentIntent.ts:60-71), not echoed from the body. The webhook independently re-validates amount+currency with paymentIntentMatchesOrder (stripeAmount.ts:20-29) for money-in events. order_id is required in payloadSchema but the handler only uses order_id.

local_checks.invariant: an already-paid or foreign-payment-method order cannot be re-charged or under-charged
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT for the recharge dimension. Filters payment_method='stripe' AND payment_status='pending' (createPaymentIntent.ts:32-33) prevent minting for paid/captured orders and for non-Stripe orders. A payment_status=pending constraint also blocks re-mint after the first capture.

local_checks.invariant: paypalCreateOrder stays bound to the original buyer-approved PayPal instrument and cannot be repointed by a later caller
local_checks.result: Amount integrity PRESENT: purchase_units amount is built server-side from order.grand_total (buildPaypalAmount with an exact minor-unit identity check, paypalPayload.ts:67-150; binding via invoice_id=order.order_number and PayPal-Request-Id=order.uuid). Binding PRESERVATION FAILS: after PayPal create, paypalCreateOrder.ts:154-157 unconditionally runs update('order').set({integration_order_id: data.id}) with no ownership predicate and no 'already-bound' guard, so a second public caller (route access 'public') can overwrite the victim order's integration_order_id with their own PayPal order. finalizePaypalOrder, paypalReturn, paypalCancel and reconcileAbandonedOrders all trust order.integration_order_id for capture/void/refund/cancel, so the repointed binding steers the money leg. See candidate paypal.createOrder.integrationOrderId.unbound.repoint.

local_checks.invariant: the PayPal return/cancel pages bind the browser token to both the order uuid and the stored integration_order_id
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT for the legitimate path: paypalReturn/index.ts:24-30 requires uuid AND integration_order_id=token AND payment_method='paypal'; paypalCancel/index.ts:26-32 adds payment_status='pending'. The binding is only as trustworthy as integration_order_id, whose integrity the unguarded overwrite above breaks.

local_checks.invariant: PaymentIntent minting must not bind to a client-supplied order uuid without an ownership predicate; amount must be server-derived.
local_checks.result: RE-VERIFIED: route is public; handler loads order only by order_id uuid + payment_method='stripe' + payment_status='pending' with no principal predicate; creates a real Stripe PaymentIntent and returns client_secret unauthenticated. NOTE (mitigant, not fix): minting a payment intent is money-out-agnostic and webhook money-in requires a real Stripe payment, so the material risk is PII enumeration + secondary fraud, not direct theft; amount is server-computed. DISPOSITION: needs_validation (runtime not executed).

local_checks.invariant: no state change happens before an authentic Stripe signature is verified
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT and fail-closed. bodyJson.ts captures the raw body (bodyParser.raw type '*/*'), and [bodyJson]webhook.ts:87-91 runs stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(request.body, sig, endpointSecret) before any DB transaction; a missing/invalid signature or an unconfigured (empty) endpoint secret throws, hitting the catch, rolling back, and returning 400 (no retry ack). No state is written before verification.

local_checks.invariant: no PayPal webhook state change happens before the producer signature is verified
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT. paypalWebhook.ts:186-210 calls PayPal's /v1/notifications/verify-webhook-signature API (webhook_id from config/settings, transmission headers + full event), and [bodyRaw]webhook.ts:46-61 rejects with 400 unless verification_status === 'SUCCESS'; an unconfigured webhook_id answers 503. The outbound verify call is an external-service fact (see validation boundaries), but the in-repo gate rejects before handlePaypalWebhookEvent.

local_checks.invariant: event object identity (PaymentIntent) binds to the local order through a server-controlled field, and unknown event types cannot drive state
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT. Events are allow-listed (isHandledPaymentIntentEvent, webhookEvents.ts:8-28); anything else is acknowledged with 200 and no mutation (webhook_lines 141-146). Result bindings are server-set at mint time (createPaymentIntent metadata.order_id) and the charge.refunded branch joins payment_transaction.transaction_id (webhook.ts:105-109,142) -- no client/browser or fabricated-envelope field keys the lookup.

local_checks.invariant: money-in events must match the bound order's amount, currency and payment method before marking paid
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT for money-in. isMoneyInEvent (succeeded / amount_capturable_updated) requires order.payment_method==='stripe' and paymentIntentMatchesOrder (exact minor-unit amount + lowercase currency, stripeAmount.ts:20-29); a mismatch is logged, acknowledged, and nothing is written (webhook.ts:169-192). Note: non-money-in branches (payment_failed, canceled) intentionally skip this match and rely solely on their status guards.

local_checks.invariant: duplicate/overlapping deliveries of money-in events do not double-emit order_placed or double-transition the order
local_checks.result: Control PRESENT. Orders are locked FOR UPDATE for the life of the webhook transaction (loadOrderByUuidForUpdate, webhook.ts:31-43/149-152); after lock, alreadyProcessed is read from payment_transaction on (transaction_id, payment_transaction_order_id) (196-200); status change and order_placed emit are skipped when alreadyProcessed; insertOnUpdate is the upsert keyed on the same pair (postgres-query-builder index.ts:1124-1141). Secondary invariants: payment_failed only downgrades a still-pending order (webhook.ts:290); charge.refunded dedupes through isRefundAlreadyRecorded on the refund id (refundStatus.ts:73-78).

local_checks.invariant: payment status transitions are ordering-safe: an event that arrives late (or for a non-authoritative intent) never downgrades a settled/captured order
local_checks.result: Control FAILS for the canceled branch. payment_failed is guarded (pending-only, webhook.ts:290) and amount_capturable_updated cannot downgrade a captured status, but payment_intent.canceled (webhook.ts:303-309) applies `updatePaymentStatus(order_id, 'canceled')` whenever payment_status !== 'canceled'. updatePaymentStatus validates only that 'canceled' is a registered status (oms/bootstrap.ts:272-276), so a stripe_captured/paypal_captured order is silently re-labeled canceled without refund, restock, shipment rollup, or order_canceled emission, bypassing the isCancelable=false gate (stripe bootstrap.ts:22-28; cancelOrder.ts validateStatus) that the admin flow enforces. See candidate stripe.webhook.canceledEvent.downgrades.settledOrder.

local_checks.invariant: A non-authoritative/late payment_intent.canceled must never downgrade a settled (stripe_captured) order.
local_checks.result: RE-VERIFIED: canceled branch writes payment_status='canceled' for any status except already-canceled including stripe_captured, via updatePaymentStatus (status-existence check only); unlike payment_failed (pending-only) it has no still-pending requirement and bypasses cancelOrder's isCancelable gate (stripe_captured registers isCancelable:false). hookAfter re-projects order.status to 'canceled' via 'canceled:*'. DISPOSITION: needs_validation (static trace confirmed; runtime not executed).

local_checks.invariant: No pull request, fork, issue comment, or external event may execute contributor-controlled code with release secrets (NPM_TOKEN, DOCKERHUB_*) or publish/mutation authority.
local_checks.result: Covered: release.yml is workflow_dispatch-only (hand-dispatched from an existing tag). checkout pins refs/tags/v$version; verify guards require the tag to equal both package.json versions, be an ancestor of origin/main, and have a changelog entry before publish may run. npm view refuses to overwrite an existing version; dry_run blocks publish/push/dist-tag/latest moves; npm provenance (id-token: write) is enabled. No untrusted-trigger path was found into the privileged jobs.

local_checks.invariant: Actions and runners used in privileged jobs are immutably pinned, and approval gates for publish are active.
local_checks.result: Hardening drift only: actions are pinned to major-version tags (checkout@v4, login@v3, build-push@v6) rather than SHAs, and the `environment: npm-publish` approval gate is commented out (lines 118-119). build_test.yml runs PR-controlled code (npm install/compile/test from the merge ref) on a hosted runner with no secrets - no privileged handoff, but its own actions (checkout@v2, setup-node@v2) are mutable. Neither rises to a confirmed candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Resolved dependencies and build inputs are immutable at the point they are consumed by a release or image build.
local_checks.result: Covered with drift note: package-lock.json is committed and npm ci is used in release; docker/Dockerfile installs @evershop/evershop@${EVERSHOP_VERSION} with --save-exact so a rebuilt image cannot silently pull a newer package; publish asserts the tarball carries declarations before publishing. Dockerfiles copy the whole tree with .dockerignore hygiene. Drift: docker-compose.yml pulls the mutable evershop/evershop:latest and postgres:16 tags (see deployment candidate/hardening). Appendix (was unresolved): Published-image provenance (cosign/sbom) and the GitHub 'npm-publish' environment existence are GitHub-hosted facts not observable in this checkout; recorded as hardening rather than a finding.
